question: Show that displacement current has the same unit as conduction current. Also explain why it can produce magnetic effects even though it is not due to actual flow of charges across the capacitor gap.

options.A:
$I_D=\varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ has unit $\text{C}^{-1}\text{ s}$, so it differs from ampere.
It produces no magnetic field because no charges cross the capacitor gap.
options.B:
$[\Phi_E]=\text{N m}^2\text{ C}^{-1}$ and $[\varepsilon_0]=\text{C}^2\text{ N}^{-1}\text{ m}^{-2}$. Therefore $[I_D]=[\varepsilon_0]\left[\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}\right]=(\text{C}^2\text{ N}^{-1}\text{ m}^{-2})\left(\dfrac{\text{N m}^2\text{ C}^{-1}}{\text{s}}\right)=\text{C s}^{-1}=\text{A}$.
A changing electric field or flux produces a magnetic field, so displacement current has magnetic effects even without charge crossing the gap.
options.C:
Displacement current has unit volt because electric flux is measured in volt metre.
It produces magnetic effects only when electrons physically cross the capacitor gap.
options.D:
Displacement current has unit tesla because it is related to magnetic field.
It produces a magnetic effect because the electric field is constant.
